subtype: Approach: trying another route when the first refuses [Revision]
passage:
Monday. Suraj went to the professor's office and asked whether the professor would guide the final-year project. "I am sorry," said the professor, "I am already handling six students and cannot give you proper time."

Tuesday. Suraj told Nilesh the news, disappointed, then said, "I should not stop there. I'll ask for a suggestion instead." Later that day Suraj sent a polite email: "Thank you for considering it. Could you suggest a colleague who works on soil sensors?"

Thursday. The professor replied with a name and a note of introduction. The new guide met Suraj and Nilesh the next week and liked the topic. Suraj wrote a thank-you back to the first professor.

qa.q: How many students was the professor already handling?
qa.a: The professor was already handling six students.

qa.q: What was Suraj feeling after the first refusal, and what did Suraj decide?
qa.a: Suraj felt disappointed but decided not to stop there, and to ask politely for a suggestion instead.

qa.q: What could Suraj try if the colleague also has no space, and why?
qa.a: Suraj could ask the department for a list of guides working on similar topics, because the topic can match more than one person.

qa.q: How might the first professor see Suraj's follow-up email?
qa.a: The professor may feel respected and glad to help by naming a colleague, since the message was polite and did not press for a yes.

grounding: When a professor is too busy to guide a project, the student politely asks for a suggestion and is pointed to a suitable colleague.

subtype: Approach: trying another route when the first refuses [Revision]
passage:
Irawati, Professor Das said no to guiding your project and you're ready to give up? Let me, Preeti, your mausi, tell you what happened to me in my final year.
I wanted Professor Chatterjee to guide my project on river pollution. I'd admired her for three years. When I asked, she said kindly that she already had eight students and couldn't take another.
I nearly walked out. My throat was tight. But at the door I turned back and asked, 'Ma'am, is there anyone you'd suggest who works on water?'
She thought for a moment. 'Dr Mondal, in chemistry. He tests river samples. Tell him I sent you.'
Dr Mondal turned out to be a better fit than she would have been. He had the equipment I needed, and he liked that I came recommended.
So go back to Professor Das. Thank him, and ask the same question.

qa.q: How many students did Professor Chatterjee already have?
How did Preeti feel when Professor Chatterjee said no?
qa.a: Preeti felt disappointed, throat tight, and nearly walked out.

qa.q: What turning point in the story led to a guide?
qa.a: Turning back at the door to politely ask for a suggestion, which led to Dr Mondal.

qa.q: How might Dr Mondal have seen a student sent by a colleague?
qa.a: He liked that she came recommended, so he was open to guiding her, and her topic fitted his work.

grounding: Shows an elder recalling a professor who was too busy to guide a project, asking politely for a suggestion and being pointed to a colleague who fitted better.

subtype: Approach: trying another route when the first refuses [Revision]
passage:
The department's deadline to register a project guide was Friday, and on Tuesday Tanvir's first choice, Dr Sarita Gill, told him she was going on sabbatical in two months and couldn't take him.
He stood in the corridor with his one-page proposal on urban heat, feeling the week collapse. Three days. Most guides were already full.
He went back in. 'Ma'am, I understand. Could you suggest anyone else whose work is close to this?'
Dr Gill read his proposal again. 'Dr Ahmed in geography maps temperature across cities. He might like this.' She wrote a two-line note on the back of the page and signed it.
Tanvir found Dr Ahmed's office on Wednesday morning, the note in hand. Dr Ahmed read both sides, asked three questions, and said, 'Friday's form, bring it here, I'll sign it.' On Friday at 3 p.m., two hours before the deadline, Tanvir handed it in.

qa.q: When was the deadline to register a guide?
What was Tanvir feeling in the corridor after Dr Gill said no?
qa.a: He felt panicked and discouraged, as if the week were collapsing with only three days left.

qa.q: What else could Tanvir have tried if Dr Ahmed had also said no?
qa.a: Ask Dr Ahmed for another name, or check with the department office which guides still had space.

qa.q: How might Dr Ahmed see Tanvir arriving with Dr Gill's note?
qa.a: Dr Ahmed sees a student vouched for by a colleague, with a topic that fits his work, which makes saying yes easy.

grounding: Shows a student, turned down by a busy professor near a deadline, politely asking for a suggestion and being pointed to a colleague who fits the topic.
